title: Mondo Duplantis breaks pole vault world record for 15th time
content:
Sweden’s Mondo Duplantis broke the pole vault world record for the 15th time at the Mondo Classic, the event named after him, on Thursday.

Once again, American-born Duplantis beat the previous world best — which he set at September’s World Championships — by a single centimetre, clearing 6.31 meters at the IFU Arena in Uppsala, Sweden.

The 26-year-old first broke the world record in February 2020 by clearing 6.17m in Orlen Copernicus Cup in Torun. He has since increased that height by 14cm, clearing by one centimetre on every occasion.

Before Duplantis’ dominant run in the sport, Renaud Lavillenie of France had held the record of 6.16m since 2014.

Duplantis typically draws fervent support across the world, such is his complete dominance in recent years. But in the country he represents internationally, the crowd was particularly buoyant when he requested the bar raised to a never-before cleared 6.31m after easing over 5.65m, 5.90m and 6.08m on his first attempts.

The bar wobbled slightly as he arched over on his first attempt, sparking wild scenes of celebration. Several of Duplantis’ rivals immediately rushed over to congratulate him on his first world record of the year, and 38th successive competition victory.

It was the second time Duplantis set a world best on home soil, having done so by clearing 6.28m in Stockholm nine months ago.

In September, the two-time Olympic gold medalist became the first men’s pole vaulter to win three straight world titles since Sergey Bubka won six in succession between 1983 and 1997.

The Mondo Classic, held in Uppsala, Sweden, invites the world’s best pole vaulters to the IFU Arena for an indoor competition in a gala format. The event is exclusively centred around pole vaulting, and takes place just over a week before the start of the World Indoor Championships in Kujawy Pomorze, Poland, where Duplantis seeks a fourth successive title.

Thursday saw a strong field in the men’s event, as Norway’s Sondre Guttormsen finished second by clearing 6.0m. American duo Zachery Bradford and Sam Kendricks finished third and fourth respectively, both clearing 5.9m. Bradford did so on his first attempt, with Kendricks requiring two.
